intent: Fix the eslint errors in bucket_catch/packages/frontend, which had never run against that package until a typecheck repair last session unmasked them, without using a single suppression and without letting the 100% coverage gate slip.
scope: 9 test files and 2 production files under bucket_catch/packages/frontend/src
45 errors down to 5; the remaining 5 are named below and left as reported findings
Non-goal: no behaviour change, no test removed, no eslint rule disabled or downgraded
changes: no-non-null-assertion (18 -> 2): in useGameLoop.test.ts and usePuzzleGameLoopPlay.test.ts the pattern was a waitFor that asserts result.current is non-null followed by several `result.current!.x` reads; replaced by capturing the value into a local and throwing if it is null, which narrows for every following line. In App.tsx `files[0]!` was simply deleted - the same position also reported no-unnecessary-type-assertion, proving the assertion changed nothing. In usePuzzleGameLoop.ts the `shift()!` became an index-then-shift, because the enclosing while condition already dereferences [0] without an assertion.

non-nullable-type-assertion-style (9 -> 0): these are the rule-swap trap - eslint asks for `!`, which no-non-null-assertion then forbids. Resolved in DropZone.test.tsx with a `must()` helper that narrows via instanceof and throws with a useful message, and in PuzzleResult.test.tsx with an inline instanceof guard.

unbound-method (10 -> 1): assertions like expect(URL.revokeObjectURL) detach a method from its object. Replaced by keeping the MockInstance handle that vi.spyOn already returns - the pattern zipDownload.test.ts was using for appendSpy/removeSpy - and asserting on that.
no-unnecessary-type-assertion (5 -> 1) and require-await (1 -> 0): dropped the redundant `as React.RefObject<T>` from three makeRef helpers, and removed `async` from a test with no await.

verification.evidence: 45 errors before, 5 after. Remaining: App.tsx no-non-null-assertion (1), usePuzzleGameLoop.ts no-non-null-assertion (1), sliceImage.test.ts no-this-alias (1) and unbound-method (1), zipDownload.test.ts no-deprecated (1). Each is explained under risks; none is suppressed.

Before: 584 statements / 217 branches / 98 functions / 535 lines, all 100%. After: 585 / 217 / 98 / 536, all still 100%. The +1 statement and +1 line are the index-then-shift edit in usePuzzleGameLoop.ts splitting one statement into two. Branches unchanged at 217 is the number that matters: no fix introduced an untested branch, which is the failure mode that would otherwise force a suppression or an unreachable guard.

verification.command: npx vitest run (via npm run coverage)
verification.evidence: 145 tests in 15 files pass, the same count as before. Every touched test file was also run individually as it was changed.
exit 0. This is the first half of `npm run lint`, and it was the step whose earlier failure had been short-circuiting the && and hiding eslint entirely.

risks: zipDownload.test.ts 'sets download attribute and href on the anchor' calls vi.restoreAllMocks() mid-test and re-spies. Moving the beforeEach spies into handles made that assertion read a stale handle and the test failed; it now keeps a local handle created after the restore. The test was already fragile in this way - the refactor made the dependency explicit rather than introducing it.

App.tsx no-non-null-assertion is NOT fixed and needs a real refactor: `fileResult!` in the done phase. Three attempts each failed the same way - a null guard adds a branch no test can reach (App's flow never produces a done phase with no result), and retagging GameResult still leaves the value nullable in the fall-through. The right fix is to move the result into the phase state (`{ kind: 'done'; result: GameResult }`), so narrowing on the phase removes the null. That is a wider change than this commit and is left for a follow-up.

usePuzzleGameLoop.ts:127 `resolvedFrameMapRef.current.get(item.id)!` is likewise unfixed: Map.get returns `| undefined` and the invariant (the id was inserted a few lines above) is not visible to the type system. A guard here would also be an unreachable branch.

sliceImage.test.ts no-this-alias: the FakeImage constructor does `capturedImg = this` so the test can drive onload. A factory breaks `new Image()`, and a Proxy wrapper passed the tests but did not reduce the error count and was more complex than what it replaced, so it was reverted. Its remaining unbound-method is on a getContext prototype save/restore.

zipDownload.test.ts no-deprecated is on the `(tag: string)` overload of document.createElement, needed because the spy must accept the signature vi.spyOn infers. Building elements from constructors instead fails under jsdom (HTMLAnchorElement is not constructible), so the deprecated overload stays.
rollback: git revert the commit. All 45 eslint errors return; nothing else changes, since no production behaviour was altered.
After rollback, confirm npm run coverage still reports 100% with 584/217/98/535 and 145 passing tests, and that npx tsc --noEmit exits 0.
